subject.title: feat(wizard): deliver progress over the RPC wizard protocol

question: Should RPC wizard progress tolerate clients that answer progress steps, or may core require all clients to re-poll without an answer?
rationale: Both behaviors are plausible protocol contracts, but current in-repo clients already answer `progress`, so accepting the strict contract would be a compatibility decision rather than a mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Preserve Progress-Answering Clients
options.body: Make progress answers harmless server-side or update bundled clients in the same rollout before broad emission.

options.title: Accept Strict Re-Poll Semantics
options.body: Require clients to re-poll without answering progress and own the compatibility rollout explicitly.

options.title: Pause Behind RPC Parity
options.body: Keep this PR paused until the broader wizard RPC parity issue settles progress-step semantics.

recommendation.title: Preserve Progress-Answering Clients
recommendation.body: Make progress answers harmless server-side or update bundled clients in the same rollout before broad emission.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses the original wizard session implementation and bundled client behavior where steipete has the strongest history signal.
